note:
R86 - Team `artid` identity space and DB-side reference graph on every committed main-database anchor (Xbox 360 08-Legacy,
PS3 08-Legacy, PS4 15-21; NHL 07 skipped - gen6 schema, no `exhibitionteams`). Read-only over `anchors/`.

Per anchor:
  identity   `exhibitionteams` (+ `leagueteams` / `customteams` where present): the `artid` field's declared depth / range, rows,
             distinct artids, duplicate artids (rows sharing one), free artids inside the declared range, sentinel-looking values
             (0, the range maximum, 255, 1000+), `index` uniqueness, the `index` -> `artid` map size; the same for `teamtype` / `custom`
             classes when the table has such a field (name containing 'type' or 'custom').
  references every field in every table whose name contains 'artid' (except `artid` on `exhibitionteams` itself, player / arena / league
             art ids): rows, distinct, non-zero values covered by the exhibitionteams artid set (fraction), the values outside it
             (first 20) - a column is a team-artid reference when coverage >= 0.95 of its non-zero values; the R14 census classes are
             cited for the 'index'-keyed references (not re-measured here).
  collision  for a hypothetical re-identification a -> b: b must be free (not held by any exhibitionteams row) and inside the declared
             range; the count of free targets per anchor; whether any artid-keyed column holds b already (a stale reference).
Usage: python r86_team_artid_graph.py <out.json>
